h: A gentle stop at the foot of Windermere
p: Lakes Aquarium is one of those easy, no-fuss visits that fits neatly into a busier Lake District day. It's compact enough to see in an hour or two, so you can enjoy it without having to plan the whole day around it, and it suits families with younger children particularly well. Little ones tend to be glued to the glass at the otters, while older kids enjoy spotting fish they might have seen while paddling or fishing in the lakes.

The local displays are the real gem. Most of us never get to see what lives in the rivers and lakes of Cumbria, and finding out about the fish, birds and other creatures beneath the surface gives you a whole new appreciation of the water you're walking beside. It's a nice way to get children thinking about wildlife and why clean lakes matter.

A few handy tips: Lakeside gets busy in peak season when boats and trains arrive, so you may find it quieter earlier or later in the day. Parking can fill up during the summer holidays, so leave a bit of extra time. It's an especially good bet when the Lakes are doing what the Lakes do best and raining.

There's lots to combine it with close by. Across the water, the National Trust's Fell Foot is a lovely lakeside park for a picnic, a paddle or hiring a rowing boat when it's open. Stott Park Bobbin Mill, run by English Heritage, shows how wooden bobbins were made for the textile industry, and it's only a short drive up the western side of the lake.
Newby Bridge itself, with its old stone bridge over the River Leven, is a peaceful spot for a short stroll before heading home or on to your next adventure.
